topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture themes, relates the content to prior practicals, and outlines the day's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cellular transformation and the discovery of oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of tumor viruses led to the identification of cellular proto-oncogenes and establish the laboratory assays used to detect cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification, pathways, and genetics of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional categories of cancer mutations and demonstrate their cellular mechanisms and allele dosage effects using the Rb pathway and p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how distinct defects in DNA repair, replication fidelity, and chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multistep tumor progression and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how sequential somatic mutations drive tumor progression and how inherited germline mutations accelerate cancer development.

topics.label: Conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture, invites questions, recommends supplementary reading, and previews the next session.
